proof_summary: Direct finite calculation shows that 43 has the required property and supplies a violating base for every \(44\le k<289\). For \(k\ge289\), write \(k=b^2+d\) with \(b=\lfloor\sqrt{k}\rfloor\) and \(0\le d\le2b\); splitting according to \(d\) produces a nearby base among \(b,b-1,b-2,b-3\) in which explicit quotient-and-remainder formulas give three pairwise distinct digits.
